candidates.name: Refeeding syndrome
support_spans: He was diagnosed with severe malnutrition and received blood transfusion; parenteral nutrition (500 kcal/day); fluids; electrolyte, trace-element, and multivitamin supplementation (including daily thiamine 100 mg IV).
Then he acutely developed profound fatigue and flaccid weakness of all four limbs.
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory values are consistent with refeeding syndrome, which occurs in severely malnourished patients who receive nutrition too quickly.

key_evidence_spans: He was diagnosed with severe malnutrition and received blood transfusion; parenteral nutrition (500 kcal/day); fluids; electrolyte, trace-element, and multivitamin supplementation (including daily thiamine 100 mg IV).
Then he acutely developed profound fatigue and flaccid weakness of all four limbs.
repeat labs showed a phosphate level of 0.05 mmol/L
He was maintained on a normal diet after bowel rehabilitation.
One month before admission, he developed diarrhea and a 7-kg weight loss with progressive weakness, anorexia, dizziness, and cachexia.
Physical examination showed pitting edema of the lower extremities, thin skin, a scaphoid abdomen, and no ascites.
ECG demonstrated normal sinus rhythm with T-wave flattening/inversion in leads II, III, aVF, and V4–V6, and an incomplete right bundle-branch block.
